newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Khmer Rouge dissidents hunt fugitive hardliners.
newsitem.headline: Khmer Rouge dissidents hunt fugitive hardliners.

text.p: Dissident Khmer Rouge commanders are hunting for senior Pol Pot loyalists who fled into the Cambodian jungles after losing their key northwestern Samlaut base earlier this week.
The dissidents, led by Ieng Sary, overran Samlaut on Monday, forcing Khmer Rouge defence chief Son Sen and Nuon Chea, hardline leader Pol Pot's right-hand man, to flee.

"We are quite sure that Nuon Chea, Son Sen and their followers are still hiding in the jungles inside Cambodia and we are hunting for them," a close aide of Ei Chien, commander of the main dissident base in Pailin, told Reuters on Friday.

The breakaway group loyal to Ieng Sary, foreign minister during the genocidal 1975-79 Khmer Rouge regime of Pol Pot, broke with the mainstream movement in August and forged a ceasefire with the government.
The dissidents believe the top hardliners are still hiding in the jungles but the Cambodian government said they may have fled across the border into Thailand.

Cambodia's second Prime Minister, Hun Sen, told reporters on Friday that he and first Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh sent a letter to Bangkok on Thursday requesting assistance in finding Son Sen and Nuon Chea.

A Thai diplomat in Phnom Penh said his government would help. "We will render all possible cooperation to the royal Cambodian government because this is an official request from the two (Cambodian) prime ministers," the diplomat, who declined to be identified, said on Friday.
He denied that the situation with the Khmer Rouge rebels was straining relations between the two countries, which have recently been at odds over nationals held in both countries.
Thai marine task forces responsible for the areas bordering Pailin and Samlaut towns denied reports that the Khmer Rouge had fled into Thailand.

"There are no reports that those people crossed the border into Thailand and we have checkpoints along the border. Anyone crossing would have been spotted by para-troopers deployed at the checkpoints," a spokesman said on Friday.
